selected.where: num = int(str(num)[::-1]) reverses the string representation of the absolute value
selected.how: Converting the reversed string back to int drops leading zeros, which were originally trailing zeros in the magnitude
selected.what: Input 120 yields (1, 1) instead of (2, 1) because the trailing zero is lost during reversal and re-parsing

selected.where: if num < 0: branch applies a transformation only to negative inputs
selected.how: The specification requires counting digits of the magnitude for all integers, but the code alters the digit sequence only for negatives
selected.what: Input -120 yields (1, 1) instead of (2, 1) due to the zero-loss bug, while positive 120 yields (2, 1) correctly
